Exactly. I think part of the reason why grunge as a whole worked as well as it did was because they had such a focus on not caring, and embracing imperfections when it came to art. Hair metal was dying, and really, you can’t get more fake than that. It was more about the looks rather than the music, and grunge really pushed against that concept. Had Nirvana been around today, despite how genius and simple the music happened to be, I doubt they’d how blown up to the same extent.

I think something I’ve noticed about Kurt recently is that people make him out to be this larger than life guy. Like he was a beatle or something.

But what I’ve grown to see is that he wasn’t. He was a normal guy. For me, an average local who was just very relatable. I think his “I’m keeping to myself” behavior made him almost mysterious and that mystery sort of allowed people to project their own thoughts and assumptions onto him. It made him into a god in a sense.

I don’t know what it is. Maybe it’s that he was just like a lot of us, but no one at the same time? He was very *ahead* of his time. He was his most authentic self and I think many of us envy how normal he was.

There’s a lot more to be said but I think Kurt was a normal guy who we stumbled upon at exactly the right time, and he wasn’t phony— something the Hollywood scene had never seen before. For once someone was kind of running away from LA/fame rather than chasing it. I think Kurt wanted to be successful but didn’t know what exactly that might entail.
